summary: A nested loop is a loop inside another loop. Use it for rows and columns: tables, patterns, and grids.
notes: The inner loop starts over from the beginning each time the outer loop moves to its next value.
print() after the inner loop, at the outer loop's indentation, ends each row.
range(row) in the inner loop makes row 1 print 1 star, row 2 print 2 stars, and so on.
pitfall: Indenting the row-ending print() one level too far puts it inside the inner loop, so every number lands on its own line.
